classification.difficultyReason: Compare rational rules to recognise a vertical translation and sketch the resulting branches and asymptotes.

spec.description: Two blue rational branches, black arrowed axes, and black dashed asymptotes labelled x=1 and y=2. No grid or origin label.
spec.mathematics: y=(2x+1)/(x-1)=2+3/(x-1); vertical asymptote x=1; horizontal asymptote y=2.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied graph is permanently visible; the requested transformed graph is absent.

inlines.text: Comparing the rules gives a new y-value 1 greater for every x.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{3x}{x-1}&=\frac{2x+1}{x-1}+1.\end{align*}$$
The translation is 1 unit up. Replace $y$ by $y-1$:
$$\begin{align*}y-1&=\frac{2x+1}{x-1}\\y&=\frac{2x+1}{x-1}+1\\y&=\frac{3x}{x-1}.\end{align*}$$
The vertical asymptote remains $x=1$, and the horizontal asymptote moves from $y=2$ to $y=3$. Both intercepts are at $(0,0)$. Translate both branches up by 1 unit.
